speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Does the pain feel more prominent on the inside, outside, or front of your knee, and do you experience any locking or giving way?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain is localized to the medial aspect of the tibia just below the kneecap, which is a classic presentation for medial patellofemoral pain syndrome or medial meniscal irritation. To distinguish between these, do you experience any clicking or catching sensations when you bend your knee, and is the pain sharp during twisting motions or more of a dull ache during straight movements?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To better assess the mechanical stability of your knee, does the knee ever feel like it is giving way or buckling, and is there any significant swelling or warmth present?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since there is no swelling or instability, this points away from a major ligament or meniscal tear and toward an overuse injury like patellofemoral pain syndrome. I would like to examine the knee for tenderness over the patellar facets and perform a patellar grind test to confirm the diagnosis.
